summary: Yingshan Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen served as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, attested in 1996, and became an honorary research fellow there upon retiring in 2023.
Yingxue Wang is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Wang earned a BA from Yale University (2013–2017) and an MA from Harvard University (2017–2025).

Yinke Chen (1890–1969) studied at Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman. A scholar of sinology, linguistics, and history, he held posts at Tsinghua, Peking University, Academia Sinica, Lingnan University, and Sun Yat-sen University.

Yinshun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and at Taisho University. He taught at the Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association, and taught at Fawang Buddhist Institute.
Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935–2018) was a philosopher. He was educated at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957–1968), and Princeton University (~1965–1966).
Yiu Wing Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Chan completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong by 2013 under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University, and Kyoto University (PhD). A specialist in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he served as a professor at the University of Haifa (~1983–2003).

Yogendra Bhardwaj specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University (2018–2021) and was appointed assistant professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2025.
Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Takatsugu Hayashi. He is attested as an associate professor at Soka University in 2026.

Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He was affiliated with Chikushi Jogakuen University as a research associate (attested 2008–2013, 2022) and was a fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda (b. 1954) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and served as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003, 2015).
Yoichi Kawada (b. 1937) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who served as director of the Institute of Oriental Philosophy, attested in 2002 and 2016.
Yong Hua is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014) under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (b. 1926) studied at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri Monastery. A Tibetology and religious studies scholar, he served as lopön at Menri and Triten Norbutse, and was a visiting scholar at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (b. 1975) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sherab Ling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and became abbot of Sherab Ling Monastery around 1992.
Yongshan He is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of James A. Benn, and also studied under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) studied at Tsinghua and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, he held posts at Southeast University, Peking University, and National Southwestern Associated University.

Yongyu Chen studied at Cornell University and Harvard University. Focusing on Buddhist studies and other fields, Chen was a professor at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015) and an ArtTable Fellow at Public Art Fund in 2025.

Yonten Gyatso (1933–2002) studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and École Pratique des Hautes Études. Specializing in Tibetology and history/archaeology, he served as research advisor for Tibetan Studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Yoshifumi Honjo (b. 1951) studied at Kyoto University. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, he taught at Kobe Women's University, served as a professor at Bukkyo University and Otani University, and joined Kyoto Bunkyo University.
